answer: I'd like to talk about the most adventurous thing I have ever done, which was a trek in the hills of Bandarban. An adventurous thing I did that pushed me well outside my comfort zone was going on a fairly challenging trek to Keokradong, one of the highest peaks in Bangladesh, with a group of four friends from university. It was about two years ago, in the dry season, when the paths are safer. I am not the most outdoorsy person, so agreeing to it was already a stretch for me. The trail was steep and [[gruelling]] in places, and at several points I genuinely wondered whether I could make it. My legs ached and my lungs burned, but my friends kept [[egging me on]]. We stopped in small villages along the way, where local people offered us water and bananas, which was incredibly kind. We spent the night in a simple guesthouse beside a lake on the way. Reaching the summit after hours of effort was absolutely [[exhilarating]], and the [[panoramic]] view of endless green hills was more than worth it. What made it so rewarding was proving to myself that I was tougher than I had believed. Honestly, I surprised myself with how much I enjoyed the challenge, despite the discomfort. That experience gave me a real taste for adventure and a newfound confidence in my own [[resilience]]. It taught me that stepping outside your comfort zone, while difficult, is often where the most memorable experiences are found. My mother, of course, was relieved to see me home in one piece.

followUps.q: Would you do something like that again?
followUps.answer: Yes, I think so, although I would train a bit beforehand this time. My friends have been talking about a trek in Nepal, and I would love to join them if work allows.

followUps.q: Do you think young people today are adventurous enough?
followUps.answer: Some are very adventurous, but many spend most of their free time on screens. I think a little adventure, even something small, builds confidence in a way that nothing online can.

note: Set on the Keokradong trek in Bandarban with university friends; added village hospitality; 'rewarding' unmarked, added 'egging me on' and 'panoramic'.
